scheme_name: Subsidy on Rehri alongwith (Stove, Gas Chulha, Utensil etc.) for the Fish/Fish Product Sale
description:
The "Subsidy on Rehri along with Stove, Gas Chulha, Utensil etc. for the Fish/Fish Product Sale" scheme is an initiative launched by the Government of India to support individuals engaged in the fish and fish product selling business.

This scheme was introduced in the year 2021 as part of the broader effort to enhance the livelihoods of fish vendors and improve the overall fish marketing infrastructure in the country.

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide financial assistance to fish vendors who operate mobile fish selling units known as "rehri."

The scheme aims to empower these vendors by providing them with essential tools and equipment necessary for their trade.

The specific goals include increasing the income of fish vendors by 20 percent within the first year of implementation.

The scheme also aims to improve the hygiene and quality of fish products sold by these vendors.

Under this scheme, eligible beneficiaries can receive a subsidy of up to 50 percent on the cost of the rehri.

The maximum subsidy amount is capped at INR 25,000 for each vendor.

In addition to the rehri, beneficiaries can also receive subsidies for essential cooking equipment.

This includes a gas chulha or stove and utensils necessary for preparing fish products.

The subsidy for the stove and utensils is also set at 50 percent of the total cost.

The maximum subsidy for these items is capped at INR 10,000.

To be eligible for this scheme, applicants must be engaged in the fish selling business.

They must be at least 18 years of age.

There is no upper age limit specified for this scheme.

The income criteria state that the annual income of the applicant should not exceed INR 3 lakh.

Applicants must also possess a valid identity proof and a bank account for subsidy disbursement.

The application process involves several steps to ensure that the beneficiaries are properly vetted.

First, applicants must fill out the application form available at designated fisheries department offices or online portals.

They must submit the completed form along with required documents.

These documents include proof of identity such as Aadhaar card or voter ID.

Applicants must also provide proof of income and a bank account statement.

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the local fisheries department.

The review process typically takes about 15 to 30 days.

If approved, the subsidy amount will be disbursed directly into the beneficiary's bank account.

The disbursement of subsidies occurs on a quarterly basis.

This means that beneficiaries can expect to receive their subsidies every three months.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

The local fisheries department at the state level is responsible for the execution of the scheme.

Contact details for local fisheries departments can be found on the official government website.

The scheme is part of a larger initiative to boost the fisheries sector in India.

The government has allocated a budget of INR 500 crore for the implementation of this scheme over a five-year period.

This budget is aimed at supporting approximately 2 lakh fish vendors across the country.

The scheme also includes provisions for training and capacity building for beneficiaries.

This training will focus on best practices in fish handling and marketing.

The government aims to enhance the skills of fish vendors to improve their business operations.

The scheme is expected to create a significant impact on the livelihoods of fish vendors.

It is also anticipated to contribute to the overall growth of the fisheries sector in India.

The fisheries sector is a vital part of the Indian economy.

It contributes approximately 1.1 percent to the national GDP.

The sector also provides employment to over 14 million people.

The government recognizes the challenges faced by fish vendors.

These challenges include competition from larger retailers and issues related to food safety.

By providing subsidies and support, the government aims to level the playing field for small vendors.

The scheme is designed to be inclusive and accessible to all eligible fish vendors.

It encourages women and marginalized communities to participate actively in the fisheries sector.

The government has also set up a grievance redressal mechanism for beneficiaries.

This mechanism allows vendors to report issues related to the application process or subsidy disbursement.

The scheme is expected to be reviewed periodically to assess its impact and effectiveness.

Feedback from beneficiaries will play a crucial role in shaping future iterations of the scheme.

The government is committed to ensuring transparency and accountability in the implementation of this scheme.

Regular audits and assessments will be conducted to ensure that funds are utilized effectively.

The scheme is aligned with the government's broader vision of promoting sustainable livelihoods.

It also aims to enhance food security by improving access to fresh fish products.

Overall, the "Subsidy on Rehri along with Stove, Gas Chulha, Utensil etc. for the Fish/Fish Product Sale" scheme is a significant step towards empowering fish vendors in India.

It provides them with the necessary tools and financial support to thrive in their business.

The scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to the welfare of small-scale fish vendors.

By addressing their needs and challenges, the scheme aims to uplift the entire fisheries sector in the country.
